projects.title: Agentic AI Based Modeling of Cattle Nutrition Systems
projects.description: Developed a data-driven, agent-based simulation in Python (using the Mesa framework) to model individual cattle nutrition, energy flow, and growth. Unlike traditional deterministic models that rely on population averages, this system simulates each animal as an independent agent with unique biological traits—improving prediction accuracy and reflecting real-world variation.The model tracks energy transformation from feed intake (Gross → Digestible → Metabolizable → Net Energy) and allocates energy hierarchically for maintenance, growth, reproduction, and storage. It integrates data logging, visualization, and environmental impact tracking (e.g., nutrient waste and methane emissions) to evaluate feed efficiency and sustainability.This framework supports researchers and producers in testing feeding and management strategies that enhance productivity while minimizing environmental impact.

We built ClinicalHours to fix the first problem. Today, we're fixing the second. Introducing ClinicalHours Premium — the pre-med platform that helps you find clinical opportunities AND turn them into a stronger medical school application. As my internship at Matic comes to an end, I’ve been thinking about how much this summer changed the way I think about product engineering. Over the past few months, I worked with Amritaraj Nair to build PulseMatic, an AI inbox management tool for physicians. We took it from an idea to a working product by understanding where physicians were losing time, identifying the problems worth solving, and laying the foundation for its integration into Matic’s flagship product, Provider AI. That process showed me what software engineering looks like in practice: build, put it in front of the team, listen to what needs to change, and come back with something better each week (shoutout sharematic). Thank you to Calvin Carter for giving me the opportunity to join Matic after our first conversation in April and to contribute alongside such a talented team throughout the summer. Thank you as well to everyone at Matic who invested their time, challenged me to think differently, and made the experience so valuable. #chickfila

We rang the gong yesterday!!! Here's what the day looked like: 8am - customer onboarding 8am - growth session 9am - plumbing company demo 10am - internal product session 12pm - customer intro 2pm - growth session 2:30pm - new customer call 3:30pm - all-hands weekly update That's one day. One Wednesday. One of our customers flew in from Salt Lake City this week to spend 3 days with us. Another is flying in today from the East Coast. Our customers don't just use our product. They come visit us. Woke up this morning to find Avinash talking to a customer at 6 am and by the time I was at my desk, we already shipped 2 great features. We shipped relentlessly since January - and fully evolved from an AI answering service to the complete AI revenue engine for the trades. We're going into deeper engagements with select customers to drive even more impact, revenue, and growth. The next few months are going to be wild. This is what it looks like when a small team decides to move fast and never stop. Throwback: Christopher rang the gong on very first day in the office!!!
